pr_title: feat(video): a one-off explainer request names its image model; the cute presets default to MiniMax image-01 and a request the site cannot draw is refused at filing
summary:
Designed against MAIN 599835f49 (every site below was re-read there; the maps' line numbers for these files still hold). No file in the repository was changed.

What the pull request does, in one line per side:
- API: `DramaRequestIn.image_model` (optional, catalog-validated, explainer family only). A cute preset that names none gets `image-01` in the schema itself, so `payload.image_model` is the one effective value: `create_one_off` stores it on the one-off series row, and the router refuses the filing with 409 when the vendor that would draw it has no key. `flat-explainer` with no model stays NULL on the row, with no key lookup, exactly as today.
- Tools: `draftEpisode` writes a top-level `image_model` into `docs/videos/<slug>/series.json` for a one-off whose row names one (and only then), which is the single fact the media stages already read; `draftBudget` tells such an explainer's writer the budget of that model.
- Web: the request form shows an image-model select for explainer presets only, preselects image-01 for a cute preset, marks an option whose vendor has no key, and vanishes when the settings read is absent. The one-off card and page show the stored model.

The disagreement the map warned about is real at MAIN and is settled by the series.json key. Traced: the server draws any picture of the episode with the row's model (`jobs.series_image_model` joins `VideoDramaEpisode.slug` to the video slug that `start_episode` sets, series.py L2610; `_model` -> `_series_image_model`, jobs.py L186-221). The worker's `draftEpisode` (flow.mjs L2171-2190) writes no top-level `image_model`, so `imageStatus` (media/stages.mjs L59-81) leaves the settings' Gemini 3 Pro choice in place: the explainer asks for a 2K picture and the server answers 422 `video_media_model_not_allowed` on every shot (image-01 sells 1K only, jobs.py L268-274; nothing is spent). On a site whose settings model has no 2K price the picture is bought and then booked failed as `video_media_model_changed` (stages.mjs L254-262). With the key written, `imageStatus` names minimax/image-01, nulls the 2K price (so 1K, US$0.0035), `imagePromptLimit` reads the server's 1,500, and the dry run prints `server: minimax image-01 ...; pictures at 1K`. media/stages.mjs, keyframes.mjs and prompt-budget.mjs need no edit.

Prompt budget, measured with prompt-budget.mjs's own arithmetic (limit - 1 - style - camera - avoid):
- cute-cartoon (style 378, negative empty): 1,093 with the longest camera word ("pan right") to 1,097 ("drift") under 1,500; 3,593 under Gemini's 4,000.
- cute-mystery (style 401, negative empty): 1,070 to 1,074 under 1,500; 3,570 under 4,000.
- flat-explainer naming image-01 (style 202, negative 204): 1,056 to 1,060.
The writer is told min(budget, 1000) = 1000 in all three cases, since a shot prompt is capped at 1000 anyway (core/drama.mjs LIMITS.prompt). The number starts to bite only when a look's style passes 471 characters; the per-shot figure in the keyframes manifest is the uncapped one.

Budget and cap: nothing has to change. A 130-picture episode at up to three takes is at most 390 picture units and 390 judge calls: US$5.27 (390 x (0.0035 + 0.01)); one take is US$1.76, in line with the three pilots' measured US$1.36-2.83. A drama-format explainer is held to `max_usd_per_video` (default 200; `capFor` uses the slides cap only for slides), far above that. The monthly limits are counts: the README recorded 6,072 of 10,000 pictures and 6,930 of 10,000 judge calls used on 2026-10-10, so the judge budget is the tighter one (about 7 worst-case or 22 typical episodes left this month). The same episode drawn by Gemini 3 Pro at 2K would be US$18.72 a take, which is what the server-side default prevents. Filing does not check the month's remaining count; a spent budget still answers 429 at draw time, as today.

No engineering default was changed. Decided inside the open points: 409 `video_drama_image_model_not_configured` (the same route's `video_drama_disabled` is the precedent: a filing the site cannot serve yet); `DramaRequestOut` does not echo the model (reason in open_items); series.json gets the key for a one-off only, never for a running long series.

changes.why: Owner decision 3: MiniMax by default for the cute looks, stored by the server. One table on the API; the worker needs none because it reads the stored value from the series row.

changes.change: (1) New field `image_model: str | None = Field(default=None, min_length=1, max_length=128)`, not added to `_trimmed`'s field list. (2) `@field_validator("image_model") @classmethod def _image_model(cls, value): return _known_image_model(value)` (the helper at L696 is resolved at call time, as SlidesSettings L250-253 already relies on): an id outside the media catalog or a retired one is a 422 with `image_model_problem`'s text. (3) A second `@model_validator(mode="after")` named `_image_model_for_preset`, placed after `_episode_length`: if `self.image_model is not None and not is_explainer_preset(self.style_preset)` raise ValueError("image_model is for an explainer preset only: a cast drama is drawn with the settings' image model, whose reference sheets hold a face across shots"); elif `self.image_model is None and (default := PRESET_IMAGE_MODELS.get(self.style_preset))` set `self.image_model = _known_image_model(default)` (so a retired default is refused by name instead of stored). An explicit `null` on a cute preset therefore also becomes image-01; `flat-explainer` with none stays None. (4) Docstring: one sentence saying an explainer may name its image model, a cute preset names image-01 when none is given, and every other preset is refused one.
changes.why: The request must carry the model, be validated like SeriesIn's (L744-755), and be explainer-only (decision 3). Putting the default in the schema mirrors `_episode_length` setting the 10-minute default and makes `payload.image_model` the single effective value for the row, the audit entry and the key check.

changes.change: In the `VideoDramaSeries(...)` call (L1291-1308) add `image_model=payload.image_model`. In the audit entry's `metadata_json` (L1335-1340) add `"image_model": payload.image_model`. Nothing else: no default logic here, no key lookup, the `VideoDramaRequest` row and `request_view(request, series_slug=slug)` unchanged. Result: cute-* with none named -> row holds "image-01"; flat-explainer or any story preset with none -> NULL as today; a named model -> that id.
changes.why: This is where the request becomes the one-off series row, and the row is already what `jobs.series_image_model` reads (jobs.py L152-161, L338), so a stored value is honoured with no change to the jobs. The audit key mirrors `add_series` (L1266).

changes.change: Add `def series_image_vendor(row: VideoAutomationSettings, model_id: str) -> str: return _series_image_model(row, model_id)[0]` with a docstring: the vendor a picture is asked of when a series names `model_id`, chosen exactly as `submit_job` chooses it (the settings' image vendor first, a retired model refused). Extend the module docstring's exception sentence: a one-off explainer whose request named a model (or took a cute preset's image-01) is drawn with it too.
changes.why: Filing must ask the same question the first picture will ask, with the same code, or the two can drift. This file is not receipt-bound; settings.py (which has a third copy of the vendor order in `slides_image_choice`) is, and is left alone.

changes.change: Import `from app.video_media.jobs import MediaJobFailed, key_for, series_image_vendor` (no cycle: jobs imports only video_automation.models and video_media.*). After the existing `drama_enabled` refusal and before `create_one_off`: `if payload.image_model is not None:` resolve `vendor = series_image_vendor(row, payload.image_model)` (a `MediaJobFailed` is re-raised as `AppError(error.status, error.code, error.detail)`; unreachable after the schema check but typed), then `if not key_for(await load_runtime_settings(session), vendor): raise AppError(409, "video_drama_image_model_not_configured", f"網站還沒有 {vendor} 的金鑰，圖片模型 {payload.image_model} 畫不了這支解說；先到 AI 設定填 {vendor} 的金鑰，或改選別的圖片模型")`. When `payload.image_model` is None nothing is looked up and nothing changes (the settings' own image vendor is already held to a key by `drama_problems` whenever the route is on, settings.py L245-272). Docstring: add the refusal. A cute-* request on a site with no MiniMax key is therefore refused, with no fallback to Gemini and nothing stored; the owner adds the key or names another model.
changes.why: Decision 3: refuse at filing, before any paid planning. 409 follows the same route's `video_drama_disabled`; the `_not_configured` suffix follows `video_media_not_configured`. `key_for` reads the same two runtime fields as `settings.configured_providers` and is literally what `submit_job` checks at L344.

changes.change: Leave all of them as they are. `DramaRequestOut` gains no `image_model` and `list_requests` no extra column. `GET /video/media/status` keeps reporting only the settings' choices.
changes.why: The page's request list shows only requests without a series (admin-video-series.tsx L490: legacy rows, whose model is always none), every new request is shown as its one-off series card from `SeriesSummary`, which already carries `image_model` (schemas.py L999, series.py L992), and the worker reads `context.series.image_model`. An echo would be a second copy nobody reads, and settings.py/models.py are receipt-bound.

A one-off with no model keeps a byte-identical series.json and its legacy cache keys (decision 4).
